# EO/IR installation kit on a CS-27 class platform

**System study — requirements, architecture, analyses and verification evidence**

Revision A. 38 requirements, 28 verification cases, 12 components, 15 declared assumptions, 13 compliance documents, 170 tests.

This is the technical report of a system study: the installation of a stabilised electro-optical and infrared payload on a light helicopter of the CS-27 class and on a tactical unmanned aircraft. The study covers the mechanical interface, the electrical interface, the balance, the field of view, the strength, the resonance, the environmental qualification plan and the compliance frame. Everything it claims is produced by a tool in this repository, pointed at by an evidence file, and re-checked by the pipeline on every change. It is not a certification, not a design release and not a flight clearance, and the report says so wherever it matters.

## R-01 — Purpose and scope

The platform is a notional normal-category light helicopter in the CS-27 class, taken as four attachment provisions on the lower fuselage, a 28 VDC bus and a declared structural environment. The payload is a notional stabilised EO/IR unit of 45 kg with a declared envelope, mounting pattern, power demand, data interfaces and field of view. Both are declared inputs in model/interfaces/, not supplier data.

The product of the study is the installation kit: the interface frame, four attachment fittings, the payload interface plate, the power and data harnesses, the circuit protection assembly, the bonding hardware, the fastener set, the connector bracket, the documentation and marking set, the environmental protection provisions and the harness routing provisions. Twelve components, listed with their masses and their requirements in model/architecture/architecture.yaml.

The study stops at the payload interface. The payload itself, the platform structure, the mission system and the maintenance programme belong to somebody else, and the report says what the study assumes about each of them instead of inventing them.

## R-02 — What this study is and what it is not

It is a traceability and analysis exercise: every requirement has a source or a declared assumption, every requirement is allocated to a component, every requirement has a verification case, and every verification case has a record that says what the evidence shows and what it does not.

It is not a certification: the compliance frame reproduces the shape of a Part 21 change assessment and stays open where the platform or the authority owns the decision. It is not a design release: the materials, the joints and the environmental categories carry declared values that a certificate or a test has to confirm. It is not a flight clearance and not an airworthiness statement of any kind.

It is also not a model of everything. The analyses are deliberately small, closed-form and checkable by hand, and each one declares the idealisation it rests on. A study that hides its assumptions in an interface between tools is worth less than one that writes them down where a reader can challenge them.

## R-03 — Method

The model is text under version control: requirements as Doorstop items, architecture, interfaces, evidence, assumptions, compliance and the analysis inputs as YAML. No figure lives in a document: it lives in the model or in an evidence file, and the documents are generated. One declaration, one calculation is the rule that makes the difference: the payload mass is declared once in the interface file, and the mass analysis, the load analysis and the report all read it from there.

Every analysis is a tool that computes, writes an evidence file and can check that the committed evidence is still what it would produce now. The pipeline runs those checks on every change, together with the tests, so the repository cannot claim a state it no longer has.

Each finding names a check, a subject, a value, a limit and a margin. A check that fails names the violated constraint; a check that passes carries the margin it passed by. That is what makes the results chapter of this report readable as a table rather than as prose.

## R-04 — The installation

The kit hangs the payload below the fuselage on four fittings that mate with the platform provisions: 900 mm longitudinal spacing, 300 mm lateral, two M8 fasteners each. The attachment geometry is checked against those provisions, because the load path divides the reaction between the four points and a geometry that does not agree with the platform would silently invalidate the structural analysis.

The layout is a two-view two-dimensional model: rectangles, circles and orthogonal harness paths in millimetres, with the platform skin as a datum. It is not a three-dimensional CAD model, and that simplification is declared rather than hidden. Everything published about the geometry is generated from it: the checks, the figure in SVG and the drawing exchange file.

The kit weighs less than the declared target with a margin, sits within the certified centre of gravity range of the platform in every declared configuration, leaves the payload field of view clear, and moves less under limit load than the clearance it has left. Those four statements are the results of four analyses, and each one is a table in the next chapter.

## R-08 — Limitations

A limitation is a statement the study cannot make, with the reason and what would close it. They come from three places: the verification cases the evidence cannot close, the open items the analyses recorded, and the assumptions still open. Each one is classified: an input is missing, the method cannot show it, it needs a physical article, it needs the platform or the authority, or it is a limitation of the review itself.

No check was relaxed to make this list shorter. Where an analysis found a problem — the antenna that sat inside the field of view, the attachment geometry that did not match the platform provisions, the inrush above the breaker rating, the resonance estimate inside the rotor bands — the problem is in this register or it was fixed in the design, and the report says which.

## R-09 — Compliance and qualification

The compliance frame follows the shape of a Part 21 change to a type design: the change classification is argued against nine criteria of appreciable effect and stays open until the design organisation confirms it, and thirteen documents cover the requirements exactly once each. The compliance matrix is generated and checked, so the coverage cannot rot quietly.

The environmental qualification plan assigns every component to an installation zone, selects the DO-160G sections that reach each zone and states, for every section, the category or the input the category waits for, the method, the article and what cannot be shown without one. The standard is not part of this repository, so no category is invented: a category is written down only where a declared input of the study and a public statement about the standard fix it.

## R-10 — Review

The review was executed against the requirement and evidence model, not against this prose: a program reads the model files and the evidence files and answers a list of review questions with checks that fail visibly. That is what makes it reproducible, and it is also its limit.

Kind: **mechanical and reproducible**. Run by: tools/report.py, run by the pipeline on every change and by the author. Independent: **no**.

What the review asks:

- Every analysis the report quotes has an evidence file that exists and reports no failure.
- Every number the repository documents quote matches the model and the evidence.
- Every limitation of the model is classified, and every classification names a real limitation.
- Every verification case that needs a future ticket points at a ticket file that exists.
- Every verification case with a passed status has an artifact that exists.
- {'No case in the register carries the warning status': 'a warning is not promoted to a pass.'}

What it found: nothing that is not already in the limitation register, and the register is checked against the model in both directions, so a limitation cannot be dropped from it and a classification cannot survive the limitation it described.

What it cannot do:

The study has one author, so this review is not independent in the sense a certification programme means. It is mechanical: every question is answered by a check that reads the model and the evidence files and fails in public, which is more than a rereading and less than a second engineer. An external review is a condition of using this material for anything other than a portfolio.

## R-11 — What remains

The study has one ticket left: publishing the package and aligning the application material with what the repository actually contains. Beyond that, the list in the limitations register is the work programme: the inputs a platform has to supply, the articles a campaign needs, and the two analyses — a modal survey and a detailed finite element model — that the closed-form idealisations cannot replace.
